data.description:
## Goal
Fix the implement skill's non-fast-forward push recovery, which crashes with NameError and strands committed work.

## Evidence
Running `implement.py finish WL-0MV4UZ6C4007XDGI` while `dev` advanced concurrently (another drive pushing) produced:

```
File ".../skill/implement/scripts/implement.py", line 4307, in phase_finish
    cwd=cwd,
NameError: name 'cwd' is not defined
```

The `PushNonFastForwardError` handler (around line 4297-4347) calls `run_cmd(["git","rebase","origin/dev"], cwd=cwd)`, but `cwd` is not defined in `phase_finish`. It should be `cwd=worktree_path` (the worktree variable used elsewhere in the function). Because the worktree is removed earlier (step 6) and the crash occurs at push (step 7), committed work is left on a local branch while the item is reset to `open`, and re-running `start` then fails because the branch already exists.

## Acceptance Criteria
- The `PushNonFastForwardError` handler rebases in the correct directory and does not raise NameError.
- A regression test covers a non-fast-forward push where `dev` advanced concurrently.
- Re-running `finish` after a non-fast-forward recovers the committed work instead of stranding it.

## Source
The skill is symlinked from `/home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents/skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` (consumer: ContextHub).

data.description:
Reduce the end-to-end cost of a post-write (cold) default-view refresh (parent WL-0MV02VA29009WBEN).

## Scope
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts`: reduce/parallelise the `wl` spawns per default-view refresh (consolidate `fetchMandatorySubsets`, `fetchActionableCount`, `fetchReviewQueueState`; extend the in-flight memo).
- Optionally read the SQLite DB in-process via `@worklog/shared` (better-sqlite3 is already a root dependency) for the default view.
- `src/read-cache.ts` / `src/read-cache-cli.ts` (only if needed): narrower invalidation / warm path. If `wl` core work grows, split it into a separate child (scope-creep mitigation).

## Acceptance Criteria
- A default-view refresh on ≥ 1000 work items and ≥ 20 expanded children completes and renders within 2 s wall-clock end-to-end, measured by the repeatable benchmark.
- The number of `wl` spawns per cold refresh is measurably reduced, verified by a spawn-count test.
- No regression for other `wl` read consumers (Pi TUI, CLI scripts); write-path correctness unchanged (no stale cache served or left behind).
- Manual verification note records the ≤ 2 s end-to-end result on this machine.

## Implementation notes
- Keep data semantics unchanged. Prefer consolidating the existing `wl list`/`next` queries before reaching into `wl` core.

## Dependencies
- F1 benchmark; F3 wiring preferred before final measurement.
